chapter: San Francisco and the postwar slump
title: Army transcriptions with Al Killian
summary: Earl Spencer's Army transcriptions where Killian's high C made the piano scream, and a Danny Kaye show with McGhee.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'd like to mention a thing that happened with Al Killian. We all played an Army transcription with the band. The guy's name was Earl Spencer. You remember he used to do the Army transcriptions, make these transcriptions for the Army to play in different parts of the world? And I'll never forget, during the recording Al Killian was sitting on the far end of the bandstand, and the piano was on the other side. And during one of those arrangements, he played a double high C, and the double high C on the piano just screamed. I had never witnessed anything like that, you
know. When he played it, the piano just screamed, as if somebody, you know, struck the key. You know? [LAUGHS]
Oh yeah, he hit it right on the money. That's intonation, you know, when those sound waves are together. And that piano just screamed out.
Yeah. It was during the Army transcriptions.

Right, right. Service transcriptions. We also did one with Howard McGhee, with Danny Kaye, his first one, right after he had made his first movie. And another singer from England made her debut on that show, Miss Beryl Davis.
Oh, she did, huh? Well, she was quite a well-liked lady when she came over.
